title: Nine at the Teeth

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: Nine times a word may come to the teeth and go back, and nine is a keeping still and not a payment. The last market sets every withholding in one square and reads a figure that does not know the hand that did not come back; what the square cannot count it calls weather, and what it cannot read it carries home in a coat.
epigraph.attribution: A proverb of Low Kiln, said at the last market of Reed

where: Low Kiln, the Weir and Sill
pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a one-hundred-and-forty-seven-to-one-hundred-and-forty-nine-day-old body carried everywhere; the surgeon's register colours the noticing (the carrying arm as a record in muscle that tells what was carried and not what it cost, a hand under a board that knows it by heart or was told not to look, a ninth sentence stopped at the word as an object on the interval tray, a sixth green and a sixth silent turn filed as a colour and a shape, a figure read aloud that is not the figure paid, the dark foot read exactly and worth nothing) without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line --- the old life stays offstage --- and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, Waiting Room, back-room interior, Marra in Sill, seventh hearing, sixth sighting of the neat dark hand, calling of the loan, spending of the seventh year or ending; the green is never Fenna in narration and the foundling is glimpsed unnamed and given no dialogue, with no loaf passed, no slate seen and no sale

scenes.title: The Last Bundles Come Out
scenes.synopsis: First entry and first dated heading of Day 147, Reed 28, Eighthday, morning going into midday at the Clay Yard and the reed beds below Low Kiln. The boy is one hundred and forty-seven days old and four months and twenty-seven days and nobody under any roof says so. The reed month has three days left and the last market and third Account-day (Reed 30, Day 149) stand two and three days off. Sella Vail carries him down at the half-pace she keeps from every open slate, giving the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket (T058/T079). The last bundles come out of the beds in armfuls judged by the arm that carried them; a cutter tells a girl with a creel that her arm knows what went into a bundle and that this is the whole of what it knows, and a man who asks what the hands will be paid is answered with the weather and the river, never a figure (T071/T072, T077). The yard goes around the clean dark line where the Ash ridge turned, the new finer grey called the thaw, the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie, and the empty place in the returning line where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out --- a look, a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried, not paid). The reed-cutter's grey cord goes past along the boards, straightened and turned where no slate lies, knotted low with teeth, put back inside his coat with the flat of the hand, knots unread (T099 carried, not paid). The boy reads the carrying arm once more as a record in muscle that tells what was carried and not what it cost: exact, complete and worth nothing, and notes the order of reaching --- the hand to the record before the hand to the person --- without standing to enter it (T061/T082). Advances T071/T072 (147 kept exact and unspent), T077, T058/T079, T009/T013/T092, T098, T099, T061/T082, and sets the last market two days off. Withheld: no figure for the hands or the reeds, no knot counted, no name, cause, body or count for the missing hand, no joining of the empty places.

scenes.title: A Finger Beneath the Board
scenes.synopsis: Second entry continued, Day 147, midday into the afternoon under the Vail kiln-house roof at the loaf shelf and the hearth. Sella sets the basket low near the bench leg at the angle at which the underside of a board becomes a roof and gives the instruction to the wool, the pot, the broom and the fire and never to the basket, telling the fire it was the thaw (T058/T079). Above, the shelf keeps its two unnamed gaps --- the old space at the row's end and the palm's breadth that came in on the night of Seed 6 with no scrape, crumb, print or word --- in a room the fold does not touch (T060/T086). The recurring wet-pot neighbour, come up from the strips with a pot set down wrong, asks what the row will want before the last market, and is sent to the pot with *Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it*, carrying the unanswered question away level so nothing slopped (T077). Standing with her back to the basket and moving her lips along the row, Sella glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and reaches a finger BENEATH the front edge where the charcoal tally lies, without looking and without a word, and brings it away and does not go back to the shelf (T100 carried, unread). The boy sees the hand go under and come back and sees nothing of what the marks say; such a hand either knows the board by heart or has been told not to look, and the reason stands between the two. He does not lay the charcoal under the shelf across the two gaps above or the one stiff crust two inches from his ear in the other room; the two rooms do not touch and no third gap comes (T097, T060/T086). The widow's mark hangs where it hangs and is not touched at a shelf or an afternoon, because neither is an opening (T079). At the hearth she tells the fire the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says *The house will keep it*, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist, the grey streak pale off the coals, and sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand (T088, T058/T079). Advances T100, T060/T086, T097, T077, T058/T079, T088, T071/T072 (147 exact). Withheld hard: no stroke counted, no figure read, no joining of the charcoal to the two gaps above it or to the crust in the fold, no third gap.

scenes.title: One Hundred and Forty-Seven
scenes.synopsis: Third entry continued, Day 147, the going of the light into the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof at the bed, the hearth and the loaf shelf seen from the basket's low angle. Sella carries him up the clay road at the half-pace, goes around a pan set out to dry and the trough by the well with its skin of ice thin as a skim of fat, goes wide around the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it, sets him on the bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without looking at his face, leaves the thread of drool frozen and unwiped, her hand resting a half-beat longer than the setting needed before it goes away, tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says *The house will keep it*, counts under her breath toward no opening and goes to her own bed without explaining the count, the two rooms not touching (T058/T079). In the small hours he turns out his file as a man lays instruments on a towel: six hearings of the full note beside and never among with no seventh invented to fill the empty place; three near-full answers advanced and not paid with Jorra's withheld knowing among them; the older intervals with the half-beat behind the standing finger, the stroke that went on without the check, his own held breath and the unchecking stroke; and EIGHT stoppings of the near-saying --- Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23 and 26 --- objects and not a rule, intervals and not payments, no payer named to any, the loan uncalled and the seventh year one tend from its end and still held (T061/T082, T036/T076). The damper's double bite is filed joined to no kiln, the two shut-room tellings stand side by side with no third, the told bell beside the heard bell (T062, T065/T095, T078). In the other room the loaf shelf keeps its two unnamed gaps and the charcoal under the board stays unread; one crust lies stiff in the fold with its empty place unnamed and no third; the word forty stays unspoken with the readable double turn beside it; the fifth green is a colour joined to no ear; the reed-cutter's cord, Mira's second twist and Orra's knot-string stay unread; Alda's six pages and both tins and Dessa's pewter tin stay shut; the soft-cuffed clerk stays set for an uncalled measure; the cold foot stays the cold to one woman and weather to the yard (T100, T060/T086, T097, T098, T099, T024/T059/T025, T050/T051, T023/T089, T090/T080, T093/T096). Through the finger's-width door comes the river's note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings; through the floor under blind ash the carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and forty-seven days; overhead the boards keep four nails, four, and a fifth that is a knot the width of a thumb --- three counts in three places and none becomes one (T088, T061/T082). Cold arrives cheek, temple, wrist, the wool riding back. One hundred and forty-seven exact and unspent and told by nobody: if somebody under that roof said the number nobody would know what it counted. He wants the crust two inches from his ear and the number spoken by somebody who would have known what a number was, and gets neither and cannot ask. His hand goes up an inch toward the note of water and comes down against the fold; in the next room the charcoal waits under the shelf for a hand not his and a day that has not come. Advances T071/T072 (147 exact), T061/T082, T036/T076 (eight stoppings held, loan uncalled), T088, T058/T079, T060/T086, T097, T098, T099, T100, T024/T059/T025, T050/T051, T023/T089, T090/T080, T093/T096, T009/T013/T092, T062, T065/T095, T078.

scenes.title: Six Where the House Can Check
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry and first dated heading of Day 148, Reed 29, Ninthday, before first grey through midday at the Vail wheel-shed, its finger's-width-open back room (not entered), the cold damper, the flagstones and the Clay Yard. Sella carries the boy past at the half-pace and gives the house no name for the men with collars high who go low-voiced into the room off the shed, and does not say the room was cold (T035/T031). Jorra comes through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger and under the nails, not bone-coloured slip, keeps dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray, asks neither which slate was broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, and the broken birth-slates under the lowest rack are entered by nobody (T035/T031, T009/T013/T092). He speaks to the wheel before anyone (*It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady*), tells a pot *You'll do*, knows its full note before it leaves the wheel and withholds the knowing from a High Kiln kiln-master who says it is singing before its time and that a pot which sings early sings itself out early (T062). Before Sella has finished telling him the fire is low his bent finger goes into the cold iron of the damper, moves the tongue a hair's breadth and leaves it standing, and the household straightens around his silence; the boy reads one piece of iron with two bites, the bite that holds a vessel whole and the bite that can take the hand off a man, with no Grathic word for both mercies, filed as an object joined to no kiln (T062). The two tellings of the counting room shut in the war stay together with no third, and the morning gives no third telling (T065/T095). Tarn takes the broom only after it has been instructed; his seventh year stands at its very edge with six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh where it cannot, the knife at the lip of its sill, the unforged collector sentence beside it, the breath from Seed 16 still unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach, and his chest tight since the dark (T036/T076). His stroke goes on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without even the half-check, and he does not turn his head along the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector; no collector comes. Neither man asks about the ear or the room and the two silences stay unjoined (T036/T076). Advances T035/T031, T062, T065/T095, T036/T076, T009/T013/T092, T058/T079, T061/T082, T071/T072 (148 kept exact). Withheld: no naming of the men, no entry of the room, no third telling, no calling word, no spending or counting of the seventh year, no collector.

scenes.title: Ask the Cord
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry continued, Day 148, midday into afternoon downriver at the Weir, the plank walk on posts, the flat blessing stone, the lower boards and below the sill at the fish-trade shade. The reed-cutter comes along the boards with the last of the bundles and the short length of grey wool or reed-fibre cord gone grey with the oil of a working thumb; he sets the bundle on the flat stone, straightens the cord, turns it once so the knots stand, ties one low with his teeth and a pull of the thumb, bites the end off and puts it back inside his coat with the flat of his hand, answering a woman who cannot read it with *You can ask the cord* and *No more can the Court*; no figure, knot, name or joining, and no laying of it beside the missing hand, Mira's cords or Orra's knot-string (T099 carried, not paid). Orra Weir stands at the lower boards with her board on its side and her hands like old rope, pale eel scars uncovered, salt white at her wrists, the grey streak first through the black hair and the nasal half-song of the Fen in her voice where she is tired; she pulls one knot down and gives a date where a figure is asked --- the ninth of Ilmen, the collector's boat round the bend on the flood with six oars and one man at the stern who never touched them --- and to *That isn't the levy*, *It's a date. The river takes what the Court doesn't. You can shout at either one. I've tried.* The forty-first double turn stays legible, tail tucked, tied left over right with the small weight of a thumb, and the word forty is unspoken (T024/T059/T025). Mira Silt works the eels with pale slime dried in long grey strokes on her sleeves and silt dried pale in the hollow of her neck, her head held a little right where the top of her left ear had been, her small smile kept like a door on the latch; asked whether the run will be thin she answers her own answer, *Thin? Who's to say thin? It comes when it comes. Ask the river*, flicks eel-bones against her thumb while deciding whether to lie and puts one away. When a buyer names a figure her thumb goes under her apron to the grey cord and stays longer than the figure required; the second cord twisted twice beneath it is never carried upriver to Nine Pots or lifted at a door, neither knot counted and the thin child's knot untouched, her board beside Orra's and not touching (T059/T025/T024). Below the sill the child's foot stays dark inside three turns of wool, the cold to the woman who wrapped it and weather to a neighbour with a pail; the surgeon's reading of the extremity going before the core, the almost-smile that is not peace and the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody will perform works perfectly and buys nothing, with no silt-leach, cause, cure or recognition written across it (T093/T094/T096 carried). The soft-cuffed clerk is still set at the out-of-line landing below the north bridge for a measure nobody called, cuff grey from washing and grey again by midday, slate to his forearm with the writing inward, hand to slate before eyes to stalls (T090/T080 carried). Sella sets the basket at the edge of the work where no slate lies and gives the instruction to the wool and the running water and never to the basket (T058/T079). Five private records stand within a dozen paces of the basket and none can be entered, side by side and not across. Advances T099, T024/T059/T025, T093/T094/T096, T090/T080, T058/T079, T071/T072 (148 exact). Withheld: no knot counted, no figure read, no word forty, no silt-leach, cause or cure, no joining of any record to the missing hand or to another.

scenes.title: Nine at the Teeth
scenes.synopsis: Sixth entry continued, Day 148, the going of the light into the small hours at the hearth and kindling under the Vail kiln-house roof. The chapter's one meaningful change. With the coals banked and the small knife set back at the very edge of its sill where it could be checked, Tarn tells the kindling *Six counted. The next I don't count* and brings the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it all the way to the word that would call the loan a NINTH time --- on Reed 29 after Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23 and 26 --- and stops there with no figure and no name. He draws the breath that should have gone in at the top of the reach and does not spend it, says *Yes, house* to the fire and goes on with the broom over the flagstones without the half-check (T036/T076). Sella, within hearing, gives the end of her instruction to the pot and asks nothing; Jorra does not ask about the ear and Tarn does not ask about the room, and the two silences stay unjoined. The boy files the ninth stopping on the interval tray beside the eight as a NINTH INTERVAL AND NOT A NINTH PAYMENT, an object among objects and not a rule, not a hearing and not a ninth hearing, refusing to let nine likenesses stand up and call themselves a doctrine --- for a doctrine is an account that has found a payer --- with no payer named to any of the nine (T036/T076, T061/T082). He holds the nine apart by hand, as he has held the eight, because a held word is a debt and a debt that can hear is a debt that can be called; the loan stays uncalled, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the seventh year one tend from its end and still not given, and the unforged collector sentence beside the knife (T036/T076). The carried fire keeps four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and forty-eight days (T088). Advances T036/T076 (ninth stopping withheld, loan uncalled), T061/T082 (ninth likeness held apart, nine not suffered to stand up as a doctrine), T058/T079, T088, T062, T065/T095, T071/T072 (148 exact). Withheld hard: no calling of the loan, no spending of the Seed 16 breath, no cutting or counting of the seventh year, no collector, no payer, no seventh hearing, no sixth green, no joining of the nine into a rule.

scenes.title: The Last Market of Reed
scenes.synopsis: Seventh entry and first dated heading of Day 149, Reed 30, Tenthday, the third Account-day of Reed and the last market of Reed, morning going into afternoon at the Cross, the reading block under the moot-post, the market stalls, the pot board, the out-of-line landing below the north bridge and the market's edge. The boy is one hundred and forty-nine days old and four months and twenty-nine days and nobody says so; the reed month goes out in the square with every withholding standing together and none read. Sella sets the basket in the moot-post's finger's width of shade where no slate lies, keeps the half-pace from every open slate and gives the instruction to the wool and the river wind and never to the basket (T058/T079). Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one corner of his mouth, wipes his thumb twice before touching nothing, holds a narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passes a finger over the figure and reads *one in twelve, as the notice says* low into the goers-by over the last bundles, calls the levy and denies it with *your house*, never *I*, says *A number goes into a slate, not a bundle. If your house wants it again, there'll be a slate at the watch*, pays two marks short for eels which the stall-keeper puts in her palm without counting where anyone can hear, and goes off up the clay road with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he has done a kindness; the figure read aloud is not the figure paid, and the figure that goes into the slate does not know the hand that did not come back (T015/T041/T047/T077, T098 carried). The bell goes four, four and a gap and nobody crosses himself, the heard bell kept beside the told bell of the Long Night (T078). Below the north bridge the soft-cuffed clerk stays set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called, hand to slate before eyes to stalls, the market sold over him as water goes over a stone (T090/T080). Across the square at the pot board a silent woman with clay under her nails, a pale line across the back of one hand and the sweetish lead-glaze green in the crease beside her lip turns a cup a quarter without lifting it and sets it back exactly where it stood, says nothing and goes off with the light: the SIXTH green at a mouth and the seventh shape of the colour counting Berr's glaze, a colour and not a name, joined to no ear and never Fenna in the narration (T050/T051 advanced, not paid). At the market's edge the foundling is glimpsed a SIXTH time, unnamed and silent and given no dialogue, in cast-off clothes worn like a uniform, silt dried pale in the creases of his wrists, a gap where a front tooth had been and a green sliver of lead glaze on a string at his throat; when a pot is set down his head goes toward it a half-beat after the boy's, after the knuckle and after the note, then stops in the middle of the turn, and he rubs the sliver twice with his thumb and opens his mouth on the tail of a kiln-hand's sentence and lets nothing out that any clerk could take down --- no loaf passed, no slate seen near the basket, no sale, the betrayal kept planted and not paid (T033/T034). The green and the half-turn are filed on places of their own beside the shelf's two gaps, the fold's crust and its gap and the field's empty place, with no joining, no fourth likeness made a cause, no third gap and no name (T050/T051, T033/T034, T060/T086, T097, T098). Advances T015/T041/T047/T077, T078, T090/T080, T050/T051 (sixth green), T033/T034 (sixth glimpse, no sale), T058/T079, T071/T072 (149 exact), T098 (carried). Withheld: the green is never a face or Fenna, the foundling is never named or given a word, no loaf, no slate, no sale, no figure read is the figure paid, no joining of any private record.

scenes.title: One Hundred and Forty-Nine
scenes.synopsis: Eighth entry continued, Day 149, the going of the light into the small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof at the bed, the hearth and the loaf shelf seen from the basket's low angle. Sella carries him up the clay road at the half-pace from every open slate, goes around a pan set out to dry and the trough with its skin of ice, goes wide around the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lie as wide as a pail of hot water set where a child might knock it, sets him on the bed and not in the Debt Loft, puts the fold right at his ear and under his chin without looking at his face, leaves the thread of drool frozen and unwiped, her hand resting a half-beat longer than the setting before it goes away; she tells the fire it was the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says *The house will keep it*, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist, the grey streak pale off the coals, sets the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, neither looks toward the bed nor touches the widow's mark, because a dusk is not an opening, and goes to her own bed without explaining the count; the two rooms do not touch (T058/T079). In the small hours he turns out his file as a man lays instruments on a towel and finds every object in its place and nothing laid across anything else: six hearings of the full note beside and never among with no seventh; three near-full answers advanced and not paid; the older intervals with the half-beat, the unchecking stroke, his own held breath; NINE stoppings of the near-saying --- Reed 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23, 26 and 29 --- objects and not a rule, intervals and not payments, no payer named to any, the loan uncalled and the seventh year one tend from its end and still held; the damper's double bite filed joined to no kiln; the two shut-room tellings with no third; the told bell beside the heard bell (T061/T082, T036/T076, T062, T065/T095, T078). In the other room the loaf shelf keeps its two unnamed gaps and the charcoal under the board stays unread; one stiff brown-edged crust lies in the fold with its empty place unnamed and no third; the word forty stays unspoken with the readable double turn beside it; the sixth green is a colour joined to no ear and the foundling a shape with no sale, never Fenna and never named in narration; the reed-cutter's cord, Mira's second twist and Orra's knot-string stay unread; Alda's six pages and both tins and Dessa's pewter tin stay shut three doors down; the soft-cuffed clerk stays set for an uncalled measure; the cold foot stays the cold to one woman and weather to the yard (T100, T060/T086, T097, T098, T099, T024/T059/T025, T050/T051, T033/T034, T023/T089, T090/T080, T093/T096). Through the finger's-width door comes the river's note of water over water, a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings; through the floor under blind ash the carried fire gives four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should have been, its payer unnamed for a hundred and forty-nine days; overhead the boards keep four nails, four, and a fifth that is a knot the width of a thumb --- three counts in three places and none becomes one (T088, T061/T082). Cold arrives cheek, temple, wrist, the wool riding back from the small bare joint. One hundred and forty-nine days old and four months and twenty-nine days, told by nobody, and if somebody under that roof said the number nobody would know what it counted. He wants the crust two inches from his ear and the number spoken by somebody who would have known what a number was, and gets neither and cannot ask. His hand goes up an inch toward the note of water and comes down against the fold, exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody, while the charcoal waits under the shelf for a hand not his and a day that has not come; the count crosses into Smoke unspent with nine held words and the loan uncalled. Advances T071/T072 (149 exact, unspent), T061/T082, T036/T076 (nine stoppings as objects, not a doctrine), T088, T058/T079, T060/T086, T097, T098, T099, T100, T024/T059/T025, T050/T051, T033/T034, T023/T089, T090/T080, T093/T096, T009/T013/T092, T062, T065/T095, T078. Nothing joined, paid, named, opened, called, spent or ended; no seventh hearing, no sixth sighting of the neat dark hand, no sale and no ending.
